handled_verified.description: Node types the analyzer reads and emits from, each pinned by a fixture in validation/m14/fixtures/nim/ (5 pass, every fixture source accepted by the Nim 2.2.12 compiler), by the 15-check index seam in script/m14/verify-nim-pipeline-e2e.ts, or by the NIM differential lane in script/m14/differential.ts (nim@60 941/941 covered, MISSING=0, unexplained=0%; pixie@60 3220/3220, MISSING=0, unexplained=0%). The declaration types are the whole surface: proc/func/method/iterator/template/macro/converter _declaration, type_declaration, variable_declaration with its const/let/var/using _section, object_declaration, enum_declaration, concept_declaration, and field_declaration / enum_field_declaration / variant_discriminator_declaration members; the call types are call and dot_generic_call; the rest are the name-, path- and argument-bearing payload nodes reached through grammar FIELDS (name, body, pragmas, module, operator, left, right, function, first_argument, type, items, source) or through node types. M14 NIM wave: no node type is matched by a source-text prefix (the analyzer contains no RegExp at all), and no field is read that the pinned grammar does not declare. Two families were found by the differential rather than by inspection and are the reason this list is evidence-backed rather than asserted: a destructuring binding (tuple_deconstruct_declaration wrapping symbol_declaration) never entered its scope frame, so a read was misattributed to a same-named struct property; and a path deeper than two segments was dropped whole because the grammar models the separator as a named `operator` node whose text is the entire token. UNIVERSAL PAIR (family convention, classified 2026-10-18): `ERROR` belongs HERE, in handled_verified, because the analyzer CONSULTS it to mark damaged output — the gate's F1 oracle appends ERROR/MISSING to every tree-sitter node census because every parser produces them without listing them in nodeTypeByNamedId. A lane that leaves them unclassified reads as two silent node types that are not silences at all.

internal_silent.description: Container, literal, comment and payload nodes that correctly emit no symbol and no relationship: they are reached by the walk and carry nothing the taxonomy has a row for. Three of these deserve the reason spelled out, because "unreferenced" is not the same as "ignored": (1) field_declaration_list and variant_declaration — a `case` block's fields are field_declaration INSIDE the variant_declaration, and the field rule emits them, so the container itself is silent while its members are handled (verified: a variant object emits properties isCircle, radius, side, name, plainField); (2) pragma_expression — a pragma wrapped around an expression contributes only its arguments, and the declaration-level pragmas are read from the `pragmas` FIELD, so this node type is a second route to the same names rather than a missing one; (3) an anonymous tuple VALUE has no name to resolve, so there is nothing for `instantiates` to point at (a NAMED construction, `TypeName(field: v)`, is handled and is the shape the corpus exercises 93 times). The `tuple_construction` NODE TYPE itself moved OUT of this bucket: in a type RHS it is the ordinary spelling of an unnamed tuple type (`type T = (int, string)`, which the compiler accepts with 0 errors), and the classifier reads it. It was misfiled here until the mutation run proved the rule behind the filing was false. The literal set (integer/float/char/nil/custom_numeric/generalized_string and their content and escape payloads) emits nothing by contract: a literal value is not a declaration and its text is not a name. The bare-statement set (assembly, bind, discard, mixin, raise, return, static, yield) declares nothing; `return`/`raise`/`yield` carry no reference the analyzer would invent a target for. UNIVERSAL PAIR (family convention, classified 2026-10-18): `MISSING` belongs HERE, in internal_silent, because it is a PARSER RECOVERY MARKER that names nothing — zero-width, no text, no symbol, no relationship can come from it. ERROR goes to handled_verified (the analyzer consults it); MISSING lands here. Neither is a gap.

gap.description: No confirmed analyzer gap: every one of the 127 named types the pinned wasm declares is either handled or a silent container, and the differential reports MISSING=0 and unexplained=0 in both directions on both corpora. The mutation gate is the second line of defence and it is what found the last two defects: 40 mutants (one per symbol kind, per relationship kind, per ruled rule, and per payload row), 27 caught on the first run, and the 13 survivors were suite holes rather than weak mutants. Chasing them found that a tuple type was never published as a struct in EITHER of the two ways Nim spells one — the grammar wraps a type RHS in `type_expression` and the classifier read the wrapper — and that an unnamed tuple element published properties named after builtin types. Both are fixed and both are now pinned in both directions, so a half-fix fails: 40/40 caught. The OPEN work in this lane is a GRAMMAR gap, which is a different ledger: 11 named node types are never reached because the pinned grammar cannot parse the construct that would produce them (do-pragma is consumed as a block comment, so no pragma node appears; a multi-line leading-dot chain, nested bracket generics `f[A, seq[B]]`, a single-line `if cond: stmt`, a `$` inside a string literal, a command-style call with a multi-line argument, a qualified type in a declaration, a pragma on a generic parameter, `func(…)` as a type, an empty tuple `(;)`, and a bare-identifier tuple construction). Those are recorded in docs/analyzers/nim.md with their site counts and named classes, and a 56-line do-pragma patch is preserved unapplied at $HOME/fixtures/nim/out/0001-nim-dopragma.patch because a rebuilt wasm has not yet passed the 72-case conformance suite, the 17-file compiler matrix and the corpus regression.

design_decision.description: Owner rulings. Each is a deliberate refusal to publish, not a silence.

decisions.question: A file-scope pragma statement (`{.push checks: off.}`, `{.warning: nil.}`) names pragmas that the analyzer does not publish anywhere. Should it?
decisions.resolution: No, and the reason is that the taxonomy has no row for a file-scope decorator: the symbols row is per declaration, and a pragma statement is not a declaration. The pragma NAMES that matter are already published — as `decorators` on each declaration that carries its own `pragmas` field, which is where they have an effect. Publishing the file-scope statement as well would produce a row whose target is a name no symbol declares, i.e. a dangling edge on purpose. Left RULED rather than silent so that the absence is a decision on the record.

decisions.question: An `overrides` edge needs the project-wide type hierarchy. The analyzer is per-file. Resolve against a corpus-wide name set?
decisions.resolution: No. A same-named method on an unrelated type is a collision, and emitting the edge would assert an inheritance relation the source never states. `overrides` is emitted only when the base is declared in the same file, which is what the fixture, the seam and the targeted 71-file method-heavy draw exercise (40 overrides, matching on both sides). The cross-file case is a declared limit of a per-file analyzer, not a gap to be papered over with a wider name set.

decisions.question: Nim has `concept`, which looks like an interface, and the base ontology has an `implements` relationship. Does a concept satisfaction emit it?
decisions.resolution: No. A concept is satisfied by implicit structural dispatch, and Nim has no nominal subtype declaration to point at, so there is no name in the file that says "X implements Y" — the fact is computed by the compiler from the method set. A concept DECLARATION is emitted as a SymbolKind.Interface symbol (it is the structural contract), but no relationship is invented for satisfaction. The differential reports the label vacuous (0 truth, 0 analyzer) rather than pretending it is covered.

decisions.question: The grammar's own file-types declares `nimble`, and 171 tracked .nimble files exist in the corpus. Route them to the nim analyzer?
decisions.resolution: YES, on measurement rather than on the grammar's file-types list — declaring a format is not evidence the analyzer models it, and routing on the declaration alone is the claim-without-coverage class. Measured over every tracked .nimble of all 12 pinned corpora: 171 files, 0 error files, 0 error nodes, 26 symbols, 315 relationships, 11 imports. 100% parse health, and a .nimble's `task`/`bin` blocks declare real things rather than being pure data, so it belongs in the symbol graph. The corpus parse record already covered these files (5,227 total, of which 5,056 are .nim/.nims); the complexity artifact measured the .nim/.nims subset and recorded the 171 .nimble share separately, so neither record silently claims the other's coverage.

decisions.question: `.nims` is a Nim configuration script, in the grammar's file-types and 65 tracked files in the corpus. Route it?
decisions.resolution: YES, and on the same measurement: 65 files, 0 error files, 0 error nodes, 43 symbols, 279 relationships, 96 imports. A .nims is NimScript — set_cmd, switch, buildFile, all procs and calls on a real stdlib — so it is Nim code by any reading that matters, and the analyzer extracts it like any other module. `src/ast/language-detection.ts` now routes .nims and .nimble to nim, and the differential and fixture lanes' ext lists were updated in the same change so the claim and the router cannot drift apart: a lane that swept an extension the router skips is the inert-pin class, and a lane that under-reports what the router now handles is the same defect wearing a hat.

excluded.label: renders
excluded.from: RULED (GRAMMAR ABSENCE — measured on the served grammar's OWN inventory, with the positive control that says the scan works, and with EVERY construct the ruling names COUNTED so the falsifier is a thing an instrument in the tree can check). THE GRAMMAR-SIDE HALF, in a DURABLE TRACKED FILE: validation/m14/measurements/nim-grammar-nodes.json records the served build's own 164 named node types over 377 ids, sha256 of the bytes the REGISTRY SERVES 421369fe6a8814dd28d0548f56dbab8877576da877b0b98ca1b905c024b5d1ad (recorded by the Lead-owned script/m14/grammar-node-inventory.ts). The filter /render|jsx|razor|element|component|markup|template|html/i matches 0 of the 164. THE POSITIVE CONTROL (L-2026-10-21-05): the SAME filter fires on 11 jsx/html node types of the javascript grammar (jsx_element, jsx_self_closing_element, jsx_opening_element, …) — a scan that finds nothing everywhere is not a scan. THE POPULATION HALF, WHOLE ADMITTED SET 6,063 files (validation/m14/measurements/nim-extended-census.json): 696 render-host-shaped calls (588 plain-identifier, 103 dot-calls), and 0 of their ARGUMENTS are capitalized identifiers, so 0 names a COMPONENT TYPE — the csharp/fsharp component predicate is 0. 1,342 calls name an HTML ELEMENT name (div/span/… 37 distinct names), which is the near miss sized: an htmlgen element macro renders an ELEMENT VALUE, never a component declaration. THE LADDER: R1 has no published alternative build to try (the served build is the pinned one); R2 would have to INVENT SYNTAX — Nim rendering is a macro DSL over ordinary `call` nodes, and the grammar has no rendering production to patch, so a patch adds a node type nothing in the language produces; R3 is vacuous in the other direction: the node type that carries a call is `call`, and publishing `renders` from a call NAME would be exactly the dart lane's impostor defect (a name filter does not separate a construct from its impostors — the declared RETURN TYPE filter is what separated dart's build methods, and no Nim construct has that shape here). FALSIFIER (a construct an instrument in the tree COUNTS): a render-host call in the admitted population whose ARGUMENT or explicit type argument names a CONCRETE COMPONENT TYPE — the census classifies every argument of every render-host call and publishes the count (measured: 0), and script/m14/nim-extended-census.ts re-computes it; OR a node type in the served build matching the render family, counted by script/m14/grammar-node-inventory.ts (measured: 0 of 164), with the javascript positive control named above. Files: validation/m14/measurements/nim-extended-census.json · validation/m14/measurements/nim-grammar-nodes.json · validation/m14/verification/NIM-EXTENDED-TYPES.md

excluded.label: mixes_in
excluded.from: RULED ONTOLOGICAL — NOT a grammar absence, and the grammar's own inventory PROVES the NAME is present: validation/m14/measurements/nim-grammar-nodes.json carries `mixin_statement` among its 164 named types, so a name-scan 'no mixin node type' ruling would be FALSE here. The reason is the SEMANTICS: Nim's `mixin` statement names SYMBOLS that are open for generic overload resolution; it composes no type into a supertype chain and declares no conformance (src/ast/types.ts:156-162 — a mixin is neither `extends` nor `implements`). THE POPULATION HALF, WHOLE ADMITTED SET 6,063 files (validation/m14/measurements/nim-extended-census.json): 75 mixin statements, 95 operands — 90 name a DECLARED ROUTINE, 4 name a declared type, 1 neither; an operand naming a type is still a symbol opened for overload resolution, not a supertype member. THE DECISIVE SEPARATION IS COUNTED: 1,047 object declarations carry the grammar's `inherits` field (`object of B`) and that construct is `extends`, already published (extends 627 edges in the arm); 337 concept declarations and 38 refinement lists are `implements`/concept refinement, already published (implements 47 edges); 448 include statements are `part_of`, published by the 2026-10-23 relabel (457 edges); 21,946 of_branch nodes are CASE-VARIANT ALTERNATIVES, not inheritance — the near miss the ruling names, sized. THE LADDER: R1 — the grammar's own inventory (164 named types) carries no with-clause/mixin-application node type and nothing in the corpus declares one; R2 — a patch would have to invent syntax: the four composition-shaped constructs Nim HAS are each already published under the truthful type (extends / implements / part_of / calls), so a patched grammar could not add a construct the language lacks; R3 — the node type that carries the closest constructs is `expression_list` under `mixin_statement`, and a `mixes_in` row from it would assert a supertype composition the source does not contain. FALSIFIER (a construct an instrument in the tree COUNTS): a mixin statement applied in a TYPE-COMPOSITION position, or a grammar node type for a with-clause/mixin application — the census counts every `mixin_statement` and every operand's class (measured 75 statements / 95 operands as above) and the inventory counts node types (0 of 164), so a non-zero in either direction refutes the ruling. Files: validation/m14/measurements/nim-extended-census.json · validation/m14/measurements/nim-grammar-nodes.json · validation/m14/verification/NIM-EXTENDED-TYPES.md

decorates._why: THE PRAGMA-TEMPLATE CLASS (rung R3, 2026-10-23). Only a declaration-owned pragma name that resolves to a FILE-LOCAL `template/macro X() {.pragma.}` emits a row; tool 30 rows over the whole population, all 30 resolved. The census's construct count is 32 candidate sites and the DELTA OF 2 IS THE CONTRACT'S 'no row when no published symbol is decorated' FILTER, measured: nim/tests/macros/tgettypeinst.nim:201 declares a type named `_` (blank identifier) carrying `{.myAttr, serializationKey.}` — this analyzer publishes no symbol for `_` (it declares nothing), so no row is invented. 294 pragma-use sites name a declared pragma template in total; the non-declaration-owned remainder is metadata, not a relationship (the 99.1 % directive class must never be swept in). The intended ONTOLOGICAL ruling was WITHDRAWN BY ITS OWN FALSIFIER: 294 applied callables in pragma positions, measured. See validation/m14/verification/NIM-EXTENDED-TYPES.md.

denominator.rule: THE DENOMINATOR IS THE LANGUAGE'S OWN EXPRESSIBLE SET, AND EVERY TYPE IS ACCOUNTED FOR: the ten canonical types are implemented, `part_of` is implemented by the R3 1:1 relabel of `include` (2026-10-23), and `decorates` is implemented by the R3 pragma-TEMPLATE class (2026-10-23 — the type was going to be RULED ontological and the census's 294 applied callables in pragma positions FALSIFIED THE RULING, which was withdrawn and replaced by the implementation; see validation/m14/verification/NIM-EXTENDED-TYPES.md). The two remaining extended types carry admissible rulings — `renders` on grammar absence with the positive control, `mixes_in` on the measured semantics of the statement that shares its name — so each leaves the denominator (the gate puts a grammar-absence OR a ruling-class exclusion into `gAbs`, which shrinks `applicable`). n = 14 − 2 = 12, and the gate RECOMPUTES n and refuses a declared denominator it cannot reproduce (script/m14/coverage-block-gate.ts: its `applicable` computation at :917 and its declared-denominator cross-check at :956). THE DONE CONDITION IS SEPARATE FROM THE RATIO: the lane is NOT DONE while a type is a gap, and it is not done while a ruling rests on a construct that has not been measured.
